segments.text: Now, in his theoretical dress, even with the sire, a sire, Jagatna or Tarkasya, while
he steps in the play of drama, acting, his way of acting is explained in next Sutra,
the 3rd chapter, 10th Sutra, Rangon Tarathma. Ranga means various ways of playing, various
parts, various parts. For instance, when he plays part of Arama, he plays part of Sita,
he plays part of Parvati, he plays part of so many things in this drama. And this playing
is three ways. One is, it is called Abhinai. Abhinai means just to copy. When you copy acting
of Rama, and the spectators must feel that you are actually Rama. Spectators must not feel
that, he is such and such person, acting as Rama. Spectators, it must be swathic Abhinai.
This is swathic Abhinai. Rajas Abhinai is, you feel something of Rama, but on the other hand,
you feel that he is such and such person, he is actor. You must know totally you know that
he is actor. This is the way how great heroes play, play part of various parts. This is called
Swathic Abhinai. Rajas Abhinai, you get hint of that, that player Rama, and the rest you feel that
he is the actor. And Tamas Abhinai is, absolutely you feel that he is actor, he is nothing else. He is
only playing as Rama, he is not actually Rama, but you must feel, spectators must feel that he is
actually Rama, playing. This is the way great heroes in this universal field act. And that hero is
here, antarathma, antar internal soul, not external soul. Ranga antarathma, ranga means the player.
The player is antarathma, internal soul. Rajatya Asmin Jagatnaati Kriya Pradeshana, Pradeshana
Aasheena Aathmanai Theranga, ranga means the playing. Jagatnaati Kriya Pradeshana Aasheena just
to reveal the universal drama. He plays in this universe just to reveal the universal drama, that this is this whole
universe is actually drama, universal drama. Tattat Bhumika Granasthanam, the place of stage where he holds the
various ways of becoming actor, various actors. One actor is Dennis, one actor is here in this universal drama, I am
another actor. And the whole universal, from universal point of view, this whole acting is done by
that internal soul. Internal soul is only one, playing part of Dennis, playing part of John, playing
part of Lakshman Ji, playing part of Andy and others. Actually, internal soul is one, and he plays
various parts in this universal drama. That is antarathma, internal self. Sanko Chowabhava Sattatta,
because he is shrunk, he is shrunk from the expansion of universality. You may call it Srinya Pradana,
Prana Pradanova, Preshta Krupo. Srinya Pramata, Prana Pramata or Preshta Pramata, not Deh Pramata,
not that soul which is residing, that is residing in wakefulness, the soul that is residing in
dreaming state or dreamless state. Tatrahi, I am Krthapadha, there he has stepped in in that field of
drama. So, Karna praspanda Krabena Jagatnatam Abhasiati, and there he puts his steps for dance and reveals
the drama of universe by infusing the spanda of his organs. Spanda means movement of organs.
Sometimes he is sad, sometimes he is vaping, sometimes he is laughing, sometimes this is how all
play. In fact, he is neither laughing nor dreaming nor sad nor joyous, he is one, as he is always.
Ukhthamcharashri Sachhande, this is already explained in Sachhande-tantra. Pureshtaka Samaaveshath,
which are on Sarviyo Nishu, antarathma, Savingaya. By entering in the subtle body of Pureshtaka,
you know Pureshtaka, Pureshtaka is that body which is found in dreaming state, that is Pureshtaka, that body.
And he enters in that Pureshtaka body and he takes the journey in each and every home in this universe.
Thus he is called antarathma. He is really antarathma interior self.
